newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen rising, focus on BOJ's 'tankan'.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen rising, focus on BOJ's 'tankan'.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract is expected to rise toward 125.00 on Wednesday after good results of Tuesday's 10-year JGB auction, traders said.

Focus is on corporate sentiment in the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) "tankan" survey due out at 8.50 a.m. (2350 GMT Tuesday). The market has discounted the BOJ's forecast for the diffusion index for major manufacturers in the June tankan of minus one, traders said.
A Reuters poll of economists produced forecasts for the DI ranging between minus four and plus four.

"The market has factored in the June DI for major manufacturers of minus one and the September DI of zero. The upward room will be limited if the actual result is the same as these," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit.
"But if the June DI is lower and the September DI is negative, a further rise toward 125.00 is likely," he said.
A dealer at a trust bank's securities unit said a worsening in the tankan may boost the September but added that its rise may be technically barred at around 125.00 for Wednesday.
If the tankan shows an improvement, that would take the market off guard and trigger aggressive selling, traders said.

"If the tankan shows an unexpected improvement and the market realises that there is possibility of higher interest rates in the October-December period, the September contract may plunge by two yen or so and fall below 123.00," the first dealer said.
